implementation: Keep the existing two- and three-argument bool function definitions and exact signatures in cli/file.hpp; add distinctly named result-returning entrypoints rather than changing signatures or adding default parameters. Use a small plain result with success, an operation enum (none/open/write/flush/close), and raw errno. The result is inspectable without parsing logs and success has none/zero error fields.

Introduce a per-call internal file-operation adapter (open, byte write, flush, close plus context) shared by production stdio and tests; avoid mutable global hooks. Preserve fopen modes w for strings and wb for buffers. String length remains strlen (stops at first NUL); use byte-count writing so string and buffer short writes have an explicit oracle. Preserve native text newline translation.

Capture errno immediately at each failed operation, before flush/close/other cleanup. Reset errno before each adapter operation so stale values cannot be attributed to a new failure; if a failing operation supplies errno=0 retain raw zero as unknown rather than inventing an OS error. Record only the earliest failure. After any successful open, attempt flush then close even after a write error, retaining earliest write/flush errors when cleanup sets different errno values. Invalidate owned handle before close so failure cannot cause retry/double close. Close failure alone must fail.

Any owned-handle destructor/cleanup is noexcept and does not publish errors by throwing; explicit completion returns the authoritative result. No new allocations or exception dependence in write/finalization path. Legacy bool wrappers use the structured result, return its success, and restore its raw first errno on failure after cleanup.

Fault adapter counts every operation and marks consumed handles; fail tests on double close or use after close. Supply distinct errno values per failure and cleanup clobbering controls.

## Original definition (verbatim)

3. **FOS-000003 — Check shared file-helper flush/close completion.** **S; no dependencies; §6.** [file:56](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/file.cpp#L56) and `write_buffer_to_file()` return true after unchecked `fclose()` (E3). Return failure for write/flush/close errors, preserving the first raw error and operation. Keep destructor/cleanup behavior nonthrowing. **Check:** `/dev/full`, nonexistent destination and successful normal write. Successful close means completion through the OS interface, not power-loss durability. This supplies a truthful primitive for later exporters.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Unit tests with injectable file operations:** Open, short-write, flush and close failures each return failure; when several occur, the first error and its operation survive cleanup. Close is attempted exactly once for each opened handle.
   - **Filesystem integration tests:** E3 fails on Linux /dev/full; a portable injected close-error case covers other platforms. Normal and empty writes succeed and read back byte-for-byte; no result claims stronger durability than tested flush/close completion.
